messages:
Alex: :rotating_light: heads up — seeing sustained egress spikes on gpu-us-east-1b-rack07. One tenant (brightlane) is pushing ~2.4Gbps out and we’re saturating the NIC queue; other tenants colocated on the same top-of-rack are hitting 95th percentile latency regressions. snippet from node: ```ifstat -i eth0 1 3
       eth0
   KB/s in  KB/s out
     0.10   2400.32
``` OpsBot: alert: egress-qos/high-queue-occupancy on gpu-us-east-1b-07 (auto-detected at 14:12 UTC) Maria: copying — any idea what brightlane was running? big model download or KV sync? Devin: they kicked a KV-prefetch job at 14:05 for a warmup sweep. pattern matches prefetch storms we saw in eu region last month. Samir: if it’s prefetch, that traffic should be on the background lane and shaped. we currently meter in sidecar but enforcement is weak for large parallel fetches. Lee: careful — moving tenants or resharing caches is non-trivial. cache warmup and cross-rack egress could increase cost and transiently spike latency for the migrated tenant. Priya: quick mitigation we can do right now: apply per-tenant egress shaping via tc in the node shim or enforce token-bucket at the sidecar outbound. we already export per-tenant egress metrics in telemetry, just missing enforcement hooks. Devin: I can push a sidecar hotfix to enforce token-bucket on the background lane (low risk). will require a controlled rollout gate and config flag. Samir: longer-term: we should add an "egress-affinity" tag to scheduler so the placement engine avoids co-locating high-egress background-heavy tenants with latency-sensitive ones on the same NIC/socket. the scheduler could treat egress as a soft constraint similar to GPU memory fragmentation. Alex: proposal / mitigation plan:
  1) immediate hotfix: sidecar outbound token-bucket for background lane (Devin)
  2) short-term: isolate brightlane onto a dedicated burst/egress pool for 24h (Ops)
  3) medium-term POC: add scheduler egress-affinity tag + placement heuristic (Samir + Maria)
  4) longer-term: billing/telemetry changes to expose egress-based billing tiers and opt-in dedicated pools (Product)
Oncall-bot: migration job created: mig-2003457001 -> target pool "burst-iso-us-east-1b" (eta ~10m) OpsBot: scheduled maintenance: node-level tc rules applying (will stagger to avoid host-wide drops) Devin: hotfix pushed to canary sidecars in us-east-1b-canary; token-bucket set to 800Mbps for background lane, shape burst size 25MB. gate: roll to 20% hosts then monitor. Alex: if we do the isolate move, please watch for inter-rack egress cost and cache miss rates. Lee: noted — I’ll set a watch for cache miss ratio and inter-AZ egress. if miss ratio > 5% for 10m, revert. Maria: quick status update: 12m after migration — 95th p50/p95 latency on impacted services back to baseline, node egress tail reduced to ~600-800Mbps. telemetry: background prefetch traffic now primarily on burst-iso pool. :thumbsup: Samir: ok this validates the affinity concept. next step, can we add a conservative scheduler constraint that prefers not to co-locate tenants with >1Gbps sustained egress on same NIC as latency tagged tenants? Lee: we should also add a cooldown to avoid thrashing (no more than 1 migration per tenant per hour). Priya: after stabilizing, I recommend we add a sidecar metric and alert: tenant_egress_sustained_seconds and a circuit that automatically throttles background lanes at 2 minutes sustained. Alex: action items captured:
  - Devin: keep hotfix in prod 48h then PR for GA rollout
  - Samir + Maria: RFC for egress-affinity scheduler with cost/perf tradeoffs (include cooldown + migration cost calc)
  - Ops: run isolated pool for brightlane for 24h and report egress cost delta
  - Lee: add cache-miss + inter-AZ egress watch and rollback automation
  - Priya: add alert rule for sustained tenant egress > 1Gbps
Oncall-bot: migration job completed successfully at 14:28 UTC. monitoring baseline restored. Alex: thanks everyone for quick response. Samir/Maria: please open RFC and include simulation of placement cost. Devin: will post canary results and follow-up rollout plan. (reaction :shipit:) Maria: opening the RFC now — will include a small simulator to estimate warmup and egress cost. closing thread after RFC created.
